title: Tanzanian Cassava in Coconut Sauce
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Muhogo wa Nazi — cassava simmered in fragrant coconut milk with garlic, turmeric, and coriander until each piece is infused with coastal sweetness and fragrance. The coastal Tanzanian cassava preparation — humble cassava transformed by coconut milk into something extraordinary.
longDesc: Muhogo wa Nazi is the Tanzanian coast's most generous treatment of cassava — simmering it in coconut milk until each piece absorbs the sweetness and fragrance of the coconut. Sold at coastal markets and served as a snack throughout the day, it is one of the great simple pleasures of coastal Tanzania.
ingredients: 600g fresh cassava — peeled and cut into chunks
steps: Peel cassava, remove woody fibre, cut into chunks.
Pre-boil in salted water for 15 minutes until nearly tender. Drain.
Combine coconut milk, water, garlic, turmeric, salt, and sugar in a pot.
Simmer gently for 10—15 minutes until cassava is completely tender and coconut sauce thickens.
chefTips: A pinch of sugar balances the coconut beautifully.
commonMistakes: Adding raw cassava directly — takes too long and over-reduces the coconut milk.
cookingScience: Pre-boiling controls cassava doneness before the coconut milk is introduced — allowing the final simmer to infuse flavour without risking the coconut milk over-reducing.
sustainabilityTips: Coastal Tanzanian cassava and coconuts — completely locally produced.
culturalNote: Muhogo wa Nazi represents the Swahili coastal philosophy — the instinct to add coconut milk to anything and make it extraordinary. Cassava becomes a celebration food with this simple addition.
